Region: Lower Galilee, between the Jezreel Valley and the coast
History: Zebulun was Jacob's tenth son, by Leah. Jacob blessed him as a haven for ships (Genesis 49:13), though his allotment in Lower Galilee never quite reached the sea. Zebulun's men fought with Deborah and Barak and are praised for risking their lives on the heights (Judges 5:18); the tribe also supplied Elon, one of the minor judges (Judges 12:11-12). Isaiah's promise of light to Zebulun and Naphtali (Isaiah 9:1) is applied to Jesus' Galilean ministry in Matthew 4. Zebulun was deported with the northern kingdom.
Culture: Zebulun's culture was that of the Galilean farming towns, trading toward the coast and the great north-south road, with a reputation for loyalty in battle disproportionate to its size.
Religion: Zebulun shared Israel's worship of the LORD, with its religious life centred on the sanctuary and later the temple.
BibleConnection: Zebulun links the judges' battlefield to the Gospels: the tribe praised for risking its life at the Kishon is named in the same Isaiah promise that Matthew applies to Jesus in Galilee.
KeyScriptures: Genesis 30:20; Genesis 49:13; Deuteronomy 33:18-19; Joshua 19:10-16; Judges 5:14; Isaiah 9:1
RelatedPeople: Zebulun; Jacob; Moses; Joshua; Deborah; Barak; Elon, Judge of Israel
